rows.measured: PASS - D6.2 CLOSES. H=4: three pi-crossings at t = 39.6858 / 79.2739 / 118.8631, half-periods 39.588/39.589 (spread 1e-3) -> T*gammadot = 15.8355, +0.81% vs Jeffery; H=8 (V1b) was +0.30%. G-wall: halving the clearance lengthens the period by +0.51 pp - the wall retards the orbit, in the direction the owner observed before, and the effect shrinks with clearance (monotone toward Jeffery). Wall-free extrapolation: an image-dipole scaling (a/l)^3 (8x per clearance doubling) puts the clearance-free period at +0.23%, an (a/l)^2 scaling at +0.13%; either way the residual at infinite clearance is +0.1..+0.25%, inside the +-3% band and of the size of the resolution/finite-Re share. The wall systematic in the certified V1b number is therefore ~0.1-0.2 pp. Other gates at H=4: modulation 4.067 (+1.7%), orientation-resolved rate slow at flow alignment (+0.30% placement, rms 0.47% of gammadot), in-plane 1.5e-8, sense correct; the figure shows the growing phase lag of the +0.81% period against the theoretical-period curve while the waveform stays on Jeffery's - exactly the discriminating picture the plot was designed for. Caveat: the H=4 mesh has h_z = 0.05 vs 0.0476 at H=8 (2b/h 10.2 vs 9.5), a 7% resolution difference that is small against the +0.51 pp shift and of the wrong sign to explain it (finer thin-axis resolution at H=4 would push the period toward Jeffery, not away). D6.2 VERDICT: the free-rotation path reproduces Jeffery's orbit at both clearances; the campaign's wall-clearance systematic is quantified rather than assumed. Optional follow-ups: V3 log-rolling start, finite-Re ladder (needs Ding & Aidun 2000). Figure: docs/md_docs/dns_figures/d62_jeffery_v2_h4.png
